Laura — quick technical summary to help legal/product: 
- Hosted inference: token/kv caches are in-memory by default and are not written to persistent disk in normal operation. We do persist checkpoints and model artifacts, but those do not contain customer prompts.
- Telemetry: We collect aggregated usage metrics (request counts, latency percentiles), and error traces that include hashed request IDs and anonymized stack traces. In urgent debugging cases we may capture a truncated input sample, but that is explicitly flagged and retained for at most 30 days. Access is restricted to SRE/ops via audit-logged tooling.
- Embeddings: There are two paths — ephemeral embeddings returned to caller only (default for API calls) and persistent embeddings when customers opt into the embeddings-store product. Persistent embeddings are stored in an encrypted datastore with customer-controlled keys if requested (Dedicated/Private).
- Subprocessors: our infra vendors (cloud regions, telemetry provider, KMS) are subprocessors; we maintain an internal list that we can export. For Dedicated/Private customers, fewer subprocessors are in scope (no hosted telemetry vendor).

Suggested contract language to propose: 
"Redwood will not persist plaintext customer inputs except where explicitly enabled by Customer (e.g., embeddings storage or log capture for debugging). Transient in-memory caches used for request routing or KV cache do not constitute persistent storage. Telemetry will be limited to aggregated, anonymized metrics; truncated request samples used for debugging will be retained for no longer than 30 days and accessed only by personnel with logged justification."

I avoided hardening exact retention windows for Dedicated customers — that's product/security decision. Happy to provide a short tech note that legal can attach.

Attachment: redwood_sec_appendix_proposal.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Thanks — Dev, that summary helps. Security position / negotiation asks: 
1) Subprocessor transparency: we should offer a maintained list (URL) and commit to 30 days' prior notice for additions that materially process customer data, with Customer right to object in writing; if Customer objects, Redwood will offer a compatible alternative (e.g., move workload to Dedicated or remove that subprocessor).
2) Telemetry & retention: agree with Dev's suggestion but tighten the debugging sample retention to 14 days for hosted to reduce surface area; for Dedicated/Private, state that telemetry vendor access is disabled unless customer opts in.
3) Embeddings: require explicit opt-in for persistent embedding storage; document flow-downs to subprocessors and KMS use. 
4) Contractual language: add a clause requiring Redwood to comply with Customer's reasonable audit requests relating to subprocessors (scope-limited and pursuant to mutual NDA).

Proposed redline snippet to send to Acme legal: 
"Redwood will maintain a current list of subprocessors at https://redwood.company/subprocessors. Redwood will provide at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice before adding any subprocessor that will materially access or process Customer Data, during which Customer may object in writing. If Customer objects, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a workable alternative (e.g., move workload to Dedicated or remove that subprocessor for that Customer's account). Telemetry collected for service health will be aggregate and anonymized; truncated request samples captured for debugging will be retained no longer than fourteen (14) days for hosted customers unless Customer consents otherwise. Persistent storage of embeddings will occur only when explicitly enabled by Customer; by default embeddings are ephemeral and returned only in the API response."

I'll attach a short note with suggested legal phrasing (sec-note-no-retention.txt). From security's side, we can accept the 30-day notification window, but want the 14-day debug-sample retention for hosted.

Attachment: sec-note-no-retention.txt (text/plain)

— Rishi
Head of Product Security

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sarah O'Connor <sarah.oconnor@acme.com>

Subject: RE: Fwd: DPA draft - subprocessor language (Acme) / action: product & security review

Sarah / Acme — thanks for the redline and callout. Internal alignment below and proposed edits we can accept on Redwood's standard DPA: 
- Subprocessor list: we will maintain a public list at https://redwood.company/subprocessors and include that link in the DPA. We will provide thirty (30) days' notice for new subprocessors that materially access Customer Data.
- Telemetry: telemetry will be limited to aggregate metrics for service health. Truncated request samples used for debugging will be retained for up to fourteen (14) days for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private customers will not have telemetry vendor access unless they opt in and may choose alternative telemetry arrangements.
- Embeddings & retention: persistent embedding storage requires explicit Customer enablement. By default, embeddings are ephemeral and returned only to the caller.
- Additional request: we'll add language that transient in-memory caches (KV caches used for inference acceleration) are not considered persistent storage.

Next steps: Laura — please send Acme legal the redline below and our proposed text. If they accept, Sales should ask for legal countersignature and we can route to DocuSign (I placed a placeholder link in the related links). If Acme requests a different retention number, come back to product/security for exception review.

Proposed text (to include in the DPA):
"Redwood will maintain a public, up-to-date list of subprocessors at the URL provided in this Agreement. Redwood will provide at least thirty (30) days' written notice prior to engaging any new subprocessor that will materially access Customer Data; Customer may object in writing and Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide alternate solutions, including migration to a Dedicated or Private deployment. Telemetry captured for service health will be aggregated and anonymized; truncated request samples captured solely for debugging will be retained no longer than fourteen (14) days for hosted customers. Persistent storage of embeddings will only occur if explicitly enabled by Customer. Transient in-memory caches used for live inference do not constitute persistent storage of Customer Data."

Laura — I'm fine signing off on this language from Product/Security. Please propose it to Acme and flag if Legal wants stricter terms; we can approve exceptions on a case-by-case basis with documented compensating controls.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product — Redwood Inference
